decided.singular: Cells shaded about 7-9 on the scale stand out against grey neighbours: day 316 (row 298, +18) is black, about 9. Days 1 and 106 and the run 152-154 are about 8. Days 105, 137, 164, 258, 273-275, 310-311, 317 and 337 are about 6-7.
decided.recurrence: Each row is 27 days, so a recurring pattern would line up vertically, and it partly does. Columns +1 to +4 are dark in rows 136, 163 and 271, and columns +12 to +14 are darker in rows 55, 82, 136, 244, 298 and 325, while other columns stay lighter. That is a moderate, imperfect 27-day alignment.
decided.quarter: Rows 271-352 hold the darkest cell (316), several more dark cells (274-275, 310-311, 317, 337-338) and a mid-grey run over about 328-334. Q2 (rows 82-163) is a close second with 106, 137, 152-154 and 164, and Q3 (rows 190-244) is visibly the lightest; with shade showing only each day's maximum, Q2 vs Q4 is near a tie.

answer.guess: Daily maximum of the geomagnetic Kp index (0-9), laid out by 27-day solar rotations (a Bartels-style chart).
